messages.author: fec32096a0f9c782
messages.subject: inla.mesh.project for ID
parts:
Hello,

As many others I am using the SPDE and follow the Cameletti paper.

So, for the mean projection of the random effect on the grid (constructed by inla.mesh.projector()) these two commands are used:
t.mean <- matrix(result$summary.random$field[,"mean"],mesh$n,T)
latent.mean <- inla.mesh.project(grid,t.mean[,1])

the result$summary.random$field has also a column ID. How can I project this column on the grid (i.e. the triangle ID of every grid point) through the inla.mesh.project() (or without it?) and keep it an integer?
or is a rounding (after the projection) sufficient? probably not....
I need the ID for a second INLA run where the grid will also be included with some lincombs, and thus the field (mesh$idx$loc) value is needed.

Thanks,
Alex

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.mesh.project for ID
parts:
Hi,

The ID column is nothing but an index, and you cannot use it for your intended purpose.

The Cameletti paper code is written to perform prediction onto a dense grid in situations where this is too much for inla to handle memory-wise. If your problem is small enough or your computer big enough to let inla handle the full prediction, I recommend replacing the prediction "stack" in the Cameletti code by your intended full prediction grid&covariates in your second in.a call. (We have written some preliminary code to automate this, but it is not yet ready for public us.)  It would also be possible to use "lincomb", but that option has drawbacks for large sparse linear combinations for implementation design reasons.  Which method is more efficient is problem dependent.

Finn
